questions.question: What defines a pair of enantiomers?

options.label: A
options.text: Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other

options.label: B
options.text: Non-superimposable mirror-image stereoisomers with opposite configurations at all stereocenters

options.label: C
options.text: Molecules that interconvert freely at room temperature

options.label: D
options.text: Isomers with different atom connectivity

questions.correct_answer: Non-superimposable mirror-image stereoisomers with opposite configurations at all stereocenters
questions.explanation: Enantiomers have identical physical properties except for the direction of optical rotation and interaction with chiral environments.

questions.question: What defines a pair of diastereomers?

options.label: A
options.text: Isomers with different molecular formulas

options.label: B
options.text: Non-superimposable mirror images

options.label: C
options.text: Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other, having different configurations at some (but not all) stereocenters

options.label: D
options.text: Conformers differing only by C-C rotation

questions.correct_answer: Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other, having different configurations at some (but not all) stereocenters
questions.explanation: Diastereomers possess different physical and chemical properties (different melting points, boiling points, and NMR spectra).

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes a meso compound?

options.label: A
options.text: An optically active 50:50 mixture of two enantiomers

options.label: B
options.text: A diastereomer lacking any stereocenters

options.label: C
options.text: An achiral molecule containing two or more stereocenters that is superimposable on its mirror image due to internal symmetry

options.label: D
options.text: A chiral molecule with zero net optical rotation

questions.correct_answer: An achiral molecule containing two or more stereocenters that is superimposable on its mirror image due to internal symmetry
questions.explanation: Despite having chiral centers, internal symmetry planes or inversion centers make meso molecules achiral.

questions.question: According to the CIP priority rules, how are substituents ranked at a chiral center?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher atomic number receives higher priority; if tied, compare atoms along the chain until the first point of difference

options.label: B
options.text: Higher molecular mass of the entire substituent receives higher priority

options.label: C
options.text: Branched chains always outrank unbranched chains regardless of atoms

options.label: D
options.text: Alkyl groups always have higher priority than heteroatoms

questions.correct_answer: Higher atomic number receives higher priority; if tied, compare atoms along the chain until the first point of difference
questions.explanation: CIP ranking strictly proceeds atom-by-atom based on atomic number.

questions.question: How is an (R) configuration determined at a tetrahedral stereocenter with lowest-priority group (4) pointing away?

options.label: A
options.text: All substituents reside in the plane of the page

options.label: B
options.text: Tracing priorities 1 -> 2 -> 3 proceeds counterclockwise

options.label: C
options.text: Tracing priorities 1 -> 2 -> 3 proceeds in a clockwise direction

options.label: D
options.text: The molecule rotates plane-polarized light in a clockwise direction (+)

questions.correct_answer: Tracing priorities 1 -> 2 -> 3 proceeds in a clockwise direction
questions.explanation: With lowest priority (4) in the back, clockwise 1->2->3 is (R) rectus; counterclockwise is (S) sinister.

questions.question: How is specific rotation [α] calculated from polarimetry data?

options.label: A
options.text: [α] = α × c × l

options.label: B
options.text: [α] = α / (molecular weight)

options.label: C
options.text: [α] = α / (c × l), where α is observed rotation, c is concentration in g/mL, and l is pathlength in dm

questions.correct_answer: [α] = α / (c × l), where α is observed rotation, c is concentration in g/mL, and l is pathlength in dm
questions.explanation: Specific rotation standardizes observed rotation against sample concentration and polarimeter cell length.

questions.question: Why does a racemic mixture exhibit an observed optical rotation of zero?

options.label: A
options.text: Enantiomers react with each other to form achiral meso complexes

options.label: B
options.text: The equal and opposite optical rotations of the two enantiomers cancel out perfectly

options.label: C
options.text: Light cannot pass through solutions of enantiomers

options.label: D
options.text: The molecules in a racemic mixture lack stereocenters

questions.correct_answer: The equal and opposite optical rotations of the two enantiomers cancel out perfectly
questions.explanation: An equimolar mixture of (+) and (-) enantiomers produces net zero rotation.

questions.question: What occurs when one of two enantiotopic protons on a CH2 group is replaced with deuterium?

options.label: A
options.text: A chiral center is created, generating one specific enantiomer

options.label: B
options.text: A meso compound is formed

options.label: C
options.text: A constitutional isomer is produced

options.label: D
options.text: No stereochemical change occurs

questions.correct_answer: A chiral center is created, generating one specific enantiomer
questions.explanation: Replacing an enantiotopic hydrogen creates a new stereocenter, generating (R) or (S) enantiomers.

questions.question: Why do simple tertiary amines (R1R2R3N) usually fail to exhibit optical activity at room temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: Nitrogen cannot form four covalent bonds

options.label: B
options.text: Amines always possess an internal plane of symmetry

options.label: C
options.text: The nitrogen lone pair prevents optical activity

options.label: D
options.text: Rapid nitrogen pyramidal inversion interconverts enantiomers faster than they can be separated

questions.correct_answer: Rapid nitrogen pyramidal inversion interconverts enantiomers faster than they can be separated
questions.explanation: Low inversion barriers (~25 kJ/mol) cause rapid umbrella-like inversion at room temperature.

questions.question: How is an (R) configuration determined at a tetrahedral stereocenter with lowest-priority group (4) pointing away?

options.label: A
options.text: The molecule rotates plane-polarized light in a clockwise direction (+)

options.label: B
options.text: Tracing priorities 1 -> 2 -> 3 proceeds counterclockwise

options.label: C
options.text: Tracing priorities 1 -> 2 -> 3 proceeds in a clockwise direction

options.label: D
options.text: All substituents reside in the plane of the page

questions.correct_answer: Tracing priorities 1 -> 2 -> 3 proceeds in a clockwise direction
questions.explanation: With lowest priority (4) in the back, clockwise 1->2->3 is (R) rectus; counterclockwise is (S) sinister.

questions.question: How is specific rotation [α] calculated from polarimetry data?

options.label: B
options.text: [α] = α / (molecular weight)

options.label: C
options.text: [α] = α × c × l

options.label: D
options.text: [α] = α / (c × l), where α is observed rotation, c is concentration in g/mL, and l is pathlength in dm

questions.correct_answer: [α] = α / (c × l), where α is observed rotation, c is concentration in g/mL, and l is pathlength in dm
questions.explanation: Specific rotation standardizes observed rotation against sample concentration and polarimeter cell length.

questions.question: Why does a racemic mixture exhibit an observed optical rotation of zero?

options.label: A
options.text: The equal and opposite optical rotations of the two enantiomers cancel out perfectly

options.label: B
options.text: Enantiomers react with each other to form achiral meso complexes

options.label: C
options.text: The molecules in a racemic mixture lack stereocenters

options.label: D
options.text: Light cannot pass through solutions of enantiomers

questions.correct_answer: The equal and opposite optical rotations of the two enantiomers cancel out perfectly
questions.explanation: An equimolar mixture of (+) and (-) enantiomers produces net zero rotation.

questions.question: What occurs when one of two enantiotopic protons on a CH2 group is replaced with deuterium?

options.label: A
options.text: A constitutional isomer is produced

options.label: B
options.text: A meso compound is formed

options.label: C
options.text: A chiral center is created, generating one specific enantiomer

options.label: D
options.text: No stereochemical change occurs

questions.correct_answer: A chiral center is created, generating one specific enantiomer
questions.explanation: Replacing an enantiotopic hydrogen creates a new stereocenter, generating (R) or (S) enantiomers.
